Let  
\[
G=(\langle v_i,v_j\rangle)_{i,j}
\]
be the Gram matrix of the basis \((v_i)\), and let  
\[
H=(\langle w_i,w_j\rangle)_{i,j}
\]
be the Gram matrix of the Euclidean dual basis. Since \(W=V^{-T}\), we have
\[
H=G^{-1}.
\]

Now define
\[
C=(\langle z_i,z_j\rangle)_{i,j}.
\]
This is the correlation matrix of the \(w_i\)’s, so \(C\) is positive definite, has diagonal entries \(1\), and has off-diagonal entries \(\pm \frac12\).

Write
\[
C_{ij}=\frac{s_{ij}}2\qquad (i\ne j),
\]
where \(s_{ij}\in\{\pm1\}\). For any three distinct indices \(i,j,k\), the corresponding \(3\times3\) principal minor is

\[
\det
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & s_{ij}/2 & s_{ik}/2\\
s_{ij}/2 & 1 & s_{jk}/2\\
s_{ik}/2 & s_{jk}/2 & 1
\end{pmatrix}
=
\frac14\left(1+s_{ij}s_{ik}s_{jk}\right).
\]

Since \(C\) is positive definite, every principal minor is positive. Hence

\[
s_{ij}s_{ik}s_{jk}=1
\]

for every triple. Therefore the signs factor as
\[
s_{ij}=\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_j
\]
for some \(\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}\). Changing \(z_i\) to \(\varepsilon_i z_i\) does not affect absolute inner products, so we may assume

\[
C_{ij}=\frac12 \quad (i\ne j).
\]

Thus
\[
C=\frac12(I+J),
\]
where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix. Since
\[
(I+J)^{-1}=I-\frac{1}{n+1}J,
\]
we get
\[
C^{-1}=2I-\frac{2}{n+1}J.
\]

So
\[
(C^{-1})_{ii}=\frac{2n}{n+1},
\qquad
(C^{-1})_{ij}=-\frac{2}{n+1}\quad(i\ne j).
\]

Because \(G=H^{-1}\), and \(C\) is obtained from \(H\) by normalizing the basis vectors \(w_i\), the off-diagonal entries of \(G\) are the normalized off-diagonal entries of \(C^{-1}\). Hence

\[
a=
\frac{\left|\,-\frac{2}{n+1}\right|}
{\frac{2n}{n+1}}
=
\frac1n.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac1n}
\]
